## How to generalize the concept of synonyms (reproducible method)

### Step-by-step approach
1) **Identify the bracketed word** and its part of speech (noun/verb/adjective).  
2) **Pick a synonym that matches the same part of speech** and fits the tone (formal/informal).  
3) **Check the local grammar** (tense, capitalization, agreement).  
4) **Re-read the sentence** to ensure the meaning is preserved.

## Multi-paragraph illustration

**Paragraph 1 (original)**  
I [drafted] a note to my friend to explain why I couldn’t make it to dinner. I wanted the message to sound calm and respectful.

**Paragraph 1 (synonyms applied)**  
I **composed** a note to my friend to explain why I couldn’t make it to dinner. I wanted the message to sound calm and respectful.

**Paragraph 2 (original)**  
I [help] by offering an alternative time to meet, and I [dislike] cancelling at the last minute.

**Paragraph 2 (synonyms applied)**  
I **assist** by offering an alternative time to meet, and I **detest** cancelling at the last minute.

**Paragraph 3 (original)**

**Paragraph 3 (synonyms applied)**

## Simple code example (synonym replacement via mapping)

```python
import re

text = """I [drafted] a note. I can [help] tomorrow.
I [dislike] cancelling. Is it [impossible] to reschedule?"""

synonyms = {
    "drafted": "composed",
    "help": "assist",
    "dislike": "detest",
    "impossible": "unattainable",
}

def replace_bracketed(text, mapping):
    def repl(match):
        word = match.group(1)
        return mapping.get(word, word)  # fallback: leave unchanged if not found
    return re.sub(r"\[([^\]]+)\]", repl, text)

print(replace_bracketed(text, synonyms))
```
